subject: Regional data housing and retention details for Hosted API — Novaterra RFI
messages:
From: Penelope Reyes <preyes@novaterra.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: procurement@novaterra.com
Date: 2028-11-21T08:12:00+00:00
Subject: Data housing / retention profile — quick clarifications

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this — we are working through the security questionnaire for our procurement review and have a few specific items on hosted API data handling we need to close out before legal signs off. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering when a customer selects an EU region?

1) Where is customer request/response content stored (region + any replicated locations)?
2) Default data retention period for request/response payloads (and whether it differs for logs/metrics/audit trails).
3) Deletion/erasures: what is the expected timeline from a customer-initiated erasure request to (a) removal from live systems/caches and (b) removal from backups?
4) Is there a contractual option to disable storing request/response content entirely for privacy-sensitive customers? If so, any performance tradeoffs?
5) List of subprocessors that may hold customer content for the hosted EU region.

We'd appreciate a concise reply that we can attach into the vendor security spreadsheet. If you need us to sign an NDA or accept a data processing addendum, say the word.

Thanks — Penelope
Penelope Reyes
Senior Security Engineer, Novaterra Systems
penelope.reyes@novaterra.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
To: Penelope Reyes <preyes@novaterra.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-11-21T10:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data housing / retention profile — quick clarifications

Hi Penelope — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary tailored to the hosted EU region; I copied Karthik (security product) and Marissa (sales operations) in case you want attachments or contractual language. We can also open a secure Drive folder with evidence.

1) Storage locations: customer request/response content for the EU region is stored within our EU cloud tenancy (primary region: eu-west-1). We do not replicate request/response payloads to non-EU regions by default. Operational data needed for routing and telemetry may cross region boundaries in anonymized/aggregated form when strictly necessary.

2) Default retention: for hosted customers the default retention for request/response payloads is 30 days. Logging and audit trails (service-level telemetry used for debugging) are retained for 90 days. Billing metering records are retained for 13 months to support invoicing.

3) Deletion/erasures: a customer-initiated erasure request triggers the following flow: immediate removal from the serving layer and KV caches within 48 hours; background purge from primary storage and metadata indexes within 7 days; removal from long-term backups is performed on the next scheduled backup cycle and completed within 30 days. We provide an erasure confirmation report when the process finishes.

4) Contractual option: enterprise customers can opt into a "no-persistence" serving mode (DPA addendum) where request/response content is not written to persistent storage — only ephemeral memory and KV caches used for inference (TTL < 1 minute). Tradeoffs: higher per-request latency and no ability to replay requests for debugging. This option is available under a dedicated contract / Dedicated plan.

5) Subprocessors: a current list for EU-hosted customers is attached (subprocessors-list-2028-11-21.pdf). Key examples: EU cloud provider (compute), EU-managed key store provider (KMS), CDN vendor for customer-facing assets. All subprocessors are contractually bound to our DPA.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-retention-summary.pdf (one-page summary you can paste into vendor spreadsheet).

If you'd like, Karthik can add the SOC2 attestation and our retention matrix in a follow-up. Let me know the deadline for procurement — we can prioritize extra evidence.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Penelope Reyes <preyes@novaterra.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: procurement@novaterra.com, legal@novaterra.com
Date: 2028-11-21T12:18:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data housing / retention profile — quick clarifications

Evelyn — this is helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups:

• For the no-persistence mode, can you confirm whether function/tool-calls and streaming responses are supported, and whether transcripts are ephemeral in the same way?
• We need to provide legal with a hard commitment on backup purge timeline for erasures (they prefer a single number they can put in the DPA). Can you provide the max window to complete backup deletion after an erasure?
• Also, procurement wants the subprocessors' country locations (not just company name) and confirmation that each has a Data Processing Agreement in place.

If possible, could you provide the SOC2 Type II attestation and a simple retention matrix CSV for our legal/procurement folks to attach?

Thanks — Penelope
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Penelope Reyes <preyes@novaterra.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-11-21T15:46:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data housing / retention profile — quick clarifications

Hi Penelope — looping in a few specifics and the artifacts you requested.

1) No-persistence mode: function/tool-calls and streaming responses are supported; transient transcripts are held only in-memory during the session and evicted immediately after the connection is closed (TTL < 60s). There is no write-to-disk in that mode. We do retain ephemeral logs for connection health (no payload). Expect a ~50–120ms increase in tail latency depending on model size because we cannot leverage certain cache optimizations.

2) Backup purge timeline (single number): we guarantee backups will be cleaned within 30 days of an approved erasure request (this is the maximum window). We include this clause in our standard DPA for EU-hosted customers.

3) Subprocessors: attached is the current list with country locations and DPA status (subprocessors-list-2028-11-21.pdf). Each listed subprocessor has an executed DPA; we rotate audits on a 12-month cadence.

Artifacts attached to this thread (secure PDFs / CSVs):
• SOC2-TypeII-attestation.pdf — latest independent attestation (redacted report header)
• data-retention-matrix-2028-11-21.csv — simple matrix showing default vs enterprise retention and deletion windows by artifact type
• subprocessors-list-2028-11-21.pdf — vendor list with country and DPA yes/no column

If you want the full SOC2 report under NDA, we can open a secure evidence folder and require a short intake form. Marissa can coordinate contract language if you want the no-persistence mode listed in the DPA.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Product, Redwood Inference
